ABB India on Friday reported a 10% year-on-year (YoY) increase in net profit to ₹440 crore for the third quarter of CY2026, while revenue grew 19% to ₹3,738 crore.
The company’s order inflows surged 56% YoY to ₹4,733 crore, marking a quarterly record. Its order backlog stood at ₹12,927 crore, up 36% from the year-ago period.
Electrification led order growth, with gains across all segments. The Motion business witnessed growth in select segments, particularly railways and services, while Automation, despite remaining muted, recorded an increase in export orders.
Key growth drivers included data centres, utilities, metals and mining, food and beverages, cement, buildings and infrastructure, the company said.
ABB India Country Managing Director Sanjeev Sharma said, “The company delivered a strong quarter, with record orders, revenue growth and a healthy backlog reflecting continued customer confidence in ABB’s technology and solutions. Demand remained broad-based across industries, supported by investments in productivity, energy efficiency and sustainable growth.”
Despite a dynamic operating environment, the company remained focused on disciplined execution and operational performance, he said.
“Looking ahead, India’s structural growth drivers in industrialisation, electrification, digitalisation and the energy transition continue to support attractive growth opportunities, positioning us well for the quarters ahead,” Mr. Sharma added.
Demand was further supported by investments in data centres, grid modernisation, renewable energy integration and energy-transition projects, alongside capital expenditure across metals, cement, railways and buildings.
